title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 16
statement: The \(5 \times 5\) grid shown contains a collection of squares with sizes from \(1 \times 1\) to \(5 \times 5.\) How many of these squares contain the shaded center square?

solutions.text:
Every \(5\times5,\) \(4\times4,\) and \(3\times3\) square contains the center cell, and there are \[ 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 = 14 \] of them.

Among the smaller squares, \(4\) of the \(2\times2\) squares and \(1\) of the \(1\times1\) squares cover the center, giving \[ 14 + 4 + 1 = 19. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Every \(3\times3,\) \(4\times4,\) and \(5\times5\) square contains the center
Then count how many \(2\times2\) and \(1\times1\) squares cover the center cell
